title: Top Canadian, U.S. trade officials meet in Washington as 50% tariffs loom | CBC News
text:
Canada-U.S. Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc and Canada's chief trade negotiator Janice Charette met with U.S. President Donald Trump's top trade envoy in Washington on Thursday.

LeBlanc was tight-lipped about his discussions with U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer as he left the afternoon meeting, saying in French that he was happy to be in the U.S. capital.

In a post on social media later Thursday, LeBlanc said the meeting was "constructive and detailed."

"Our focus has been and will continue to be on striking a comprehensive deal that addresses sectoral tariffs and benefits Canadian workers, farmers and businesses," he said.

The meeting was slated to only last 30 minutes, but LeBlanc was in the trade office for an hour and a half. It was the second time LeBlanc and Charette have sat down with Greer in as many weeks.

Two sources with knowledge of the plans told CBC News that LeBlanc will be in Washington again next week.

This latest sit-down comes after Prime Minister Mark Carney said trade talks would "intensify" after Trump threatened fresh tariffs on hundreds of Canadian imports starting Aug. 19.

Trump calls Canada 'nasty' — and Carney responds

Carney said earlier this week that negotiators are focusing talks with their U.S. counterparts on "all strategic sectors," including autos, as that new deadline approaches. The prime minister reiterated that position on Thursday.

"We're interested in a more comprehensive deal, a global deal that addresses the strategic sectors," he told reporters in Saguenay, Que.

"Will we get all of that by the 19th of August? We'll see. But we want to have pathways in order to get that."

Carney needs to 'focus on the results that he promised' in trade talks with the U.S.: Poilievre

Last month, Carney said he'd spoken with Trump and the two leaders agreed to ramp up trade discussions.

Former Quebec premier Jean Charest, who serves on Carney's Advisory Committee on Canada-U.S. Economic Relations, shed light on that phone call in an interview with CBC's Power & Politics, saying it resulted in wider engagement from the U.S. administration in the latest round of talks.

"It's a good sign that the whole of the administration is more engaged in these negotiations than they were before that phone call," he told guest host Katie Simpson.

Should Canada's trade negotiators change tack?

Despite the ongoing talks, Trump took a jab at Canada on Wednesday night during a rally in Las Vegas.

"I love tariffs, right? Because we've been screwed by tariffs used against us for years. By China, by Japan, by South Korea, by Germany, by everybody, by Canada," Trump said, as the crowd cheered.

"Canada's nasty. They are. They're nasty," he added. "I love the people, but they're nasty. Nasty leadership."

Canada-U.S. trade minister back in Washington as countries 'intensify' trade talks

Trump's new tariff threat shows Canada's retaliation 'being noticed': Ontario's D.C. rep

Canada doesn't 'get credit' for rolling back trade irritants, U.S. envoy says

Carney brushed off Trump's comment when asked about it on Thursday.

"Whatever adjective is used, we're standing up for Canadian workers, for Canadian businesses," he said.

Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre called out Carney's handling of the tariff dispute during a news conference on Thursday, saying, "It's time to get results."

"We're calling on him to take the leverage that he has not yet squandered, take it to the bargaining table and get something in return for a change," Poilievre said.

Senior writer

Darren Major is a senior writer for CBC's parliamentary bureau in Ottawa. He previously worked as a digital reporter for CBC Ottawa and a producer for CBC's Power & Politics. He holds a master's degree in journalism and a bachelor's degree in public affairs and policy management, both from Carleton University.
